title: Jason Calacanis #AskJason: low-cost marketing, protecting ideas, focus, and knowing when to quit
summary: Jason answers Reddit/Quora founder questions with his CMO. He covers low-cost offline marketing (meetups, street teams, podcasts), why unique ideas matter less than execution, keeping early momentum by studying feature usage data, and testing willingness to pay before burning five years on a startup.

principles.text: Beat paid-ad costs with real-world exposure: meetups, street teams and freebies that also yield product feedback.
principles.quote: real-world exposure to products is a great hack and you can very simply compare it to the cost of your online acquisitions

principles.text: Don't broadcast your idea before executing; people who do the work win credibility over people who talk.
principles.quote: you want to be in the bucket of people who do the work not the stalkers

principles.text: You don't need a unique idea; win on unique strategic, tactical and execution decisions plus timing.
principles.quote: you do not have to have a unique idea what you need to have is unique strategic tactical and execution ideas

principles.text: Keep momentum by plotting features by usage frequency and share of users, then focus ~90% of attention on the top ones.
principles.quote: you should put 90 percent of your attention towards whatever those number one and number two features are

principles.text: Stay focused on your core group and compound small daily gains instead of chasing side projects.
principles.quote: turn those 300 people into 303 or 307 and if you're doing that every day and you're adding you know one percent a day

principles.text: If a product hasn't worked in five years, force users to pay or engage to find out if there's a business.
principles.quote: if it hasn't worked in five years it's likely that it's not gonna work out
